set.typical_award_size: Regulatory requirement and the County's only local housing revenue. Ordinance 6050-B (October 27, 2020), effective January 1, 2021: new private residential projects of more than 100 units must make 10% of units affordable; projects of 8 to 100 units may instead pay an in-lieu fee per habitable square foot of each market-rate unit. The fee was $2.00 initially and is indexed; the Board's April 7, 2026 annual impact fee adjustment raised it from $2.73 to $2.84 per square foot effective July 1, 2026. An Employee Accommodation Fee of $2.84 per net building square foot applies to new non-residential development in the Sierra Nevada and Lake Tahoe area (Tahoe Truckee Unified School District boundary). Exempt: projects of 7 or fewer units or where most units are under 1,600 square feet, deed-restricted affordable housing, ADUs, infill sites, transit priority areas, mixed-use projects at least 70% residential, and others in Section 15.65.050. Fee revenue funds construction of affordable housing, preservation, acquisition-rehab of multifamily projects and first-time homebuyer assistance.
set.affordability_requirement: 10% of units affordable for projects over 100 units, with the in-lieu fee option for 8 to 100 units; compliance terms set in a development agreement or affordable housing agreement. A BAE Urban Economics nexus study update (draft, not approved) and ordinance amendments are scheduled on the County's project page for a Board update in fall or winter 2026 to 2027 and final Board adoption in spring or summer 2027.
eligible_project_detail: market-rate residential projects of 8 or more units in unincorporated Placer (compliance)
fee revenue funds new construction, preservation, acquisition-rehab and first-time homebuyer assistance
set.cycle_notes: Not an application program. Requirement applies at entitlement; the fee is calculated at complete building permit application and paid before permit issuance. Fee is adjusted annually by the Board (current $2.84 per square foot from July 1, 2026).
set.next_deadline: No application deadline; applies at entitlement with fee paid before building permit issuance. Nexus study and ordinance amendments are scheduled for final Board adoption in spring or summer 2027 per the County project page as of November 8, 2026.
set.layering_notes: For a 100% affordable or deed-restricted project the ordinance is not a cost (exempt). For a mixed-income project over 100 units it is a 10% set-aside; between 8 and 100 units the fee is $2.84 per square foot (about $2,840 on a 1,000 square foot unit), low relative to Bay Area counties. The fee revenue is the pool behind the County's gap loans, so a higher fee from the 2027 nexus update would expand the only local source. The infill and transit priority area exemptions remove many western Placer multifamily sites from the requirement. Density bonus and inclusionary agreements do not trigger prevailing wage. placer.ca.gov program pages opened directly on November 8, 2026.
set.audit_note: Replaced news-article source with the County program page; fee updated to $2.84; funding_type changed from density bonus to regulatory requirement per SCHEMA meanings; nexus adoption moved to 2027.

reason: County page shows the fee rose to $2.84 effective July 1, 2026 and the nexus update slipped to 2027; the record was also misclassified as density bonus.

set.typical_award_size: County formula allocations confirmed on HCD documents: 2019-2023 five-year estimate $2,730,542 (2024 amended formula NOFA); 2019 allocation award $455,090 on October 21, 2020 (activities 1 and 9); 2022 and 2023 allocations ($385,467 and $247,060, total $632,527 with $31,626 admin) awarded April 30, 2026 for activity 9 only. HCD's CY 2024-2028 Formula Allocation NOFA (July 16, 2026) lists Placer County at $489,950 (CY 2024) and $538,105 (CY 2025), about $3,062,188 over five years. Cities receive their own allocations.
set.affordability_requirement: 2024-2028 PLHA Formula Guidelines Section 301: rental activities up to 120% AMI (150% in high-cost areas), owner-occupied workforce housing up to 120% AMI, homelessness assistance up to 30% AMI; rental development assistance must be a low-interest deferred loan with a regulatory agreement of at least 55 years. The County's 2019-2023 plan used activity 1 (multifamily rental) in 2020 but only activity 9 (homeownership opportunities including down payment assistance) for the 2022-2023 award.
set.cycle_notes: Formula grant to the County from HCD. The County must adopt a 2024-2028 five-year plan and apply to HCD; CY 2024 funds released spring 2026 with an HCD application deadline at the end of February 2028, CY 2025 by February 2029. Any developer competition is a County decision; the County last ran a developer NOFA in 2020.
set.next_deadline: No open County PLHA developer round as of November 8, 2026. The County's HCD application for its CY 2024 allocation is due February 29, 2028 (final business day of February 2028).
set.prevailing_wage_basis: The 2024-2028 PLHA Formula Guidelines (https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/plha/2024-2028-plha-formula-guidelines.pdf) contain no prevailing wage provision; coverage of a County PLHA loan is a Labor Code 1720 question, including the 1720(c)(6)(E) affordable housing exemption applied in DIR PW 2006-020.
set.layering_notes: At about $500,000 a year, County PLHA is modest. The 2022-2023 allocations awarded April 30, 2026 went to homeownership activity 9, not multifamily rental, so a developer should ask the Economic Development and Housing Division to include rental activities and a developer NOFA in the 2024-2028 plan. Prior record text saying state funds trigger prevailing wage had no cited rule.

reason: HCD award lists and the 2024-2028 NOFA confirm the dollar figures but show the 2022-2023 County award went to homeownership only, the AMI rules changed under the 2024-2028 guidelines, and no rule supports prevailing wage true.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: DIR Decision on Administrative Appeal, PW 2006-020 Heber Family Apartments (https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-020(A).pdf), following PW 2004-016 Rancho Santa Fe: loans of conduit tax-exempt bond proceeds (publicly offered or privately placed) and federal LIHTCs are not payment out of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b). Other public loans in the same deal are evaluated separately.

reason: Staff report at the redirected URL matches award, AMI and schedule; prevailing wage set to false on the DIR conduit bond determination.
